F-R67-1.what: the previous session did not stop cleanly -- it was terminated mid-flight. task_plan.md's closing section describes I-14-D(r3) and I-14-E-APPLY as 'dispatched, results not yet collected', which reads as 'running elsewhere'.
F-R67-1.evidence: I-14-E-APPLY/a20260921-01/after/bench.log last arm line EXIT=3221225786 (= 0xC000013A STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT, i.e. terminated, NOT a business failure); the next line starts arm B4-nonvacuity-quiet whose log is 0 bytes; no write for the following 8 minutes; no live python process
F-R67-1.generalisation: 'results not yet collected' != 'results being produced' -- the two are indistinguishable from the wording alone, so a closing claim that something is in flight must be checked against a production path (live process / growing log / on-disk intermediate)

F-R67-2.what: execution_runs/B5-plan-level-remediation/ was UNTRACKED AS A WHOLE DIRECTORY, containing the 34764 B reviewer_report.md that is the sole carrier of the B5 review verdict
F-R67-2.why_worse_than_the_known_mode: T1-27's registered failure mode is 'an append block lives only in the working tree' -- but an append block at least has a COMMITTED BASE to replay from. An untracked directory has no base at all.

F-R67-3.what: the closing section records 8 unpushed commits; the measured value is 10 (two more landed after the section was written: 6d62b046, 1bddfc1e)
F-R67-3.reading_discipline: the unpushed count must be recomputed on the spot with git rev-list --left-right --count <upstream>...HEAD; it is independent of how far progress.md has been written, so the ledger's position cannot be used to infer it

F-R67-4.what: STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT (3221225786) is not a failure code
F-R67-4.generalisation: it only says someone terminated the process; reading it as 'the test failed' attributes a failure to an arm that never finished. Correct conclusion is 'not completed', not 'not passed' -- the same distinction the frozen rc table draws between rc=2 (no verdict) and rc=3 (judged and failed).
